results.title: Get started: ask your AI about your data · freddy help
results.content:
## Questions to try

- "How did I sleep this week compared with last week?"
- "Which of my runs this month had the highest average heart rate?"
- "Is there a pattern between my late workouts and my sleep?"

## Where your health questions go

Ask your health questions in your AI app. It reads your data through freddy and answers there.

Use Support for help with freddy itself: a connection, a sync, your account or your plan. freddy AI answers first, and a person from the team can take over. Neither can read or explain your health values. See Get help in support chat.

Related: Choose a source · Your AI app shows an error or no data [...] freddy holds your health and performance data. Your AI app reads it and answers your questions.

## Four steps

When you make a new account, freddy opens a setup with four steps. Each step shows where you are, for example "Step 2 of 4".

1. Connect a source. Choose your watch, ring, app or Apple Health. Other sources lists the rest, with search. See Choose a source.
2. Bring in your data. Your first data comes in. Choose Continue when you do not want to wait.
3. Connect an AI app. Follow the steps for Claude, ChatGPT or another app.
4. Ask. Ask your AI app the question that freddy shows.

When you start in ChatGPT or Claude, the AI app step is done, so you start at Step 2 of 4.

Choose Skip for now to stop. Finish setting up freddy in Next steps on the Overview takes you back.

results.title: freddy Launches the Health Data Server: One Home for All Personal Health Data
results.content:
freddy stores each value with the unit, time and time zone the source gave. When a source deletes or replaces a record, freddy does the same. The private link works with any client that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP), such as Claude or ChatGPT. Users can export every stored value as a CSV file, and developers can build on the Personal API and the open-source CLI. Stored data is encrypted at rest, and every AI read is logged.

freddy is CASA certified by an independent security lab. It never sells user data and never uses it to train AI models. When a user deletes their data, freddy deletes it. [...] Most people now hold their health data in several apps: a ring for sleep, a watch for training, a glucose monitor, a gym log, a lab portal. Each app shows its own part. freddy connects these sources once and keeps every value as the source sends it, with no scores and no changes. The user then chooses how to use it: with any AI assistant through one private link, as a full download, or through the Personal API.

freddy connects 20 sources directly, plus more than 180 apps through Apple Health and Health Connect. Direct sources include Garmin, Oura, Polar, Suunto, Withings, Apple Health, Health Connect and Google Health. New: users can add lab results from a lab report through their AI and see them in one table, and the Personal API is open to build on. freddy has more than 20,000 users. [...] "Every device and app shows you one dimension of your health: your ring sees your sleep, your watch sees your training, your lab report sees your blood. You need all of it in one place, in full depth and breadth, before you or your AI can reason about the whole picture and make truly informed decisions," said Tom Tomaszewski, founder of freddy.

freddy is available now at freddy.coach and on the App Store and Google Play.

Overview

freddy connects wearable, fitness, glucose, strength-training, and environmental data to ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, coding agents, and other MCP-compatible clients. Its provider credentials and Personal API are read-only, so it does not write health or workout data back to connected services. Its MCP surface can still perform account actions such as connecting, disconnecting, or syncing a provider when the user requests them.

results.title: freddy Launches the First Health & Performance Context Layer for LLMs | Fitt Insider
results.content:
AI assistants can reason about almost anything, except you. They have no idea how you slept, how hard you trained, what your glucose did overnight, or even the air you’re breathing. freddy fixes that. Today freddy announced general availability of the first health context layer for large language models, a single private connection that lets any AI assistant read your own health data.

freddy is not just a wearable connector. It brings together the full picture of a person’s health: rings and watches like Oura, Garmin, WHOOP and Polar; training platforms like Hevy, Strava and Intervals.icu; continuous glucose monitors; smart scales and body composition; and home sensors that track your air quality and sleep environment. [...] freddy is built on a simple principle: people should own the context about their own bodies. Users grant access to their own accounts through each provider’s official login, and freddy reads that data on their behalf. It does not broker, resell, or pool data across users, and any connection can be revoked at any time and data deleted with one click.

The launch lands as AI assistants and personal health converge. Major platforms have signaled that conversational AI will become a primary interface for health, but most efforts are locked to a single assistant or a single device ecosystem. freddy is source-agnostic and assistant-agnostic by design, a neutral context layer that sits between everything a person measures and the AI they ask. [...] “An AI assistant can reason about almost anything, except you,” said Tom Tomaszewski, founder of freddy. “It doesn’t know how you slept, how hard you trained, or what your glucose did last night. freddy gives it that context, from your wearables to your training to the air in your bedroom, and soon your bloodwork. Connect your sources once, then talk to your own data the way you’d talk to a coach.”

freddy is available today at freddy.coach.
